headline: Fuel prices jump by Tk 20 per litre across Bangladesh, sparking inflation fears
summary: The government announced the hike, effective midnight Sunday, citing international market increases and significant losses by BPC. Consumers Association of Bangladesh warns of extreme difficulty for people to cope.
details: The government has increased fuel prices by Tk 20 per litre, effective from Sunday midnight, a move that the Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB) warns will make it extremely difficult for people to survive. This hike follows a period of significant losses for the state-owned Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) due to rising international oil prices.

Under the new rates, diesel will sell for Tk 135 per litre, petrol for Tk 160, octane for Tk 165, and kerosene for Tk 155. These new prices were announced in a gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Power, Energy, and Mineral Resources.

This is not the first increase this year; on April 18, diesel prices rose by Tk 15 to Tk 115 per litre, petrol by Tk 19 to Tk 135, octane by Tk 20 to Tk 140, and kerosene by Tk 18 to Tk 130. Further increases of Tk 5 for petrol, octane, and kerosene followed in June.

With inflation already exceeding 8%, experts like CAB's energy advisor M Shamsul Alam fear this fuel price hike will exacerbate the situation. Alam noted that after electricity and now fuel, gas prices might also increase, making survival extremely challenging for the general populace.

Alam highlighted that while government employees received a 100-144% salary increase, the majority of the population faces dire economic conditions. He questioned how the government expects to collect taxes if people lose purchasing power, suggesting that the revenue loss might outweigh the reduced subsidies.

The Energy Division justified the hike by stating that despite abnormal international price increases, domestic fuel prices remained unchanged for the past five months. They also pointed out that fuel prices in neighboring countries are significantly higher than in Bangladesh.

The division attributed the international price surge to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has more than doubled fuel prices and shipping costs since March. This led to BPC incurring a loss of Tk 22,876 crore between March and August. The BPC is currently losing approximately Tk 89 per litre on diesel, amounting to about Tk 109 crore daily, projecting an annual loss of nearly Tk 40,000 crore on diesel alone.

By increasing fuel prices by Tk 20 per litre, the government aims to reduce BPC's annual losses by approximately Tk 10,000 crore. The Energy Division also cited the risk of fuel smuggling to neighboring countries if prices remain significantly lower in Bangladesh, noting that diesel in Kolkata costs Tk 135 per litre, Myanmar Tk 165, Nepal Tk 161, Sri Lanka Tk 179, Thailand Tk 151, and Pakistan Tk 185.

Bangladesh experienced its largest single fuel price hike in August 2022, when diesel increased by Tk 34 to Tk 114 per litre, later reduced by Tk 5 after public criticism. That previous hike significantly drove up commodity prices and transport fares, a scenario feared to repeat now.

headline_marked: [[Case filed against MP Gazi Nazrul]] and 2 others over second wife’s death in Dhaka
headline: Case filed against MP Gazi Nazrul and 2 others over second wife’s death in Dhaka
summary: Mariam Khatun's hanging body was recovered from a NAM Bhaban flat. Her father filed the case, naming the MP, his first wife, and Mariam's maternal uncle as accused.
details: A case has been filed against Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and two others on charges of abetting the death of his second wife, Mariam Khatun. Mariam’s hanging body was recovered from a flat at NAM Bhaban in Dhaka last night.

Mariam’s father, Masum Billah, filed the case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station late Sunday night. Gazi Nazrul’s first wife, Maksuda Begum, and Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman were also named as accused.
Police stated that Gazi Nazrul was present at the flat when Mariam’s body was recovered. Following this, he and Maksuda were taken to the police station for questioning regarding the incident.

Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Ibne Mizan clarified that the MP has not been arrested in the case. As a lawmaker, he is subject to specific legal procedures before an arrest can be shown, but questioning is ongoing.
